items.title: The sheaf of relative differentials is canonically isomorphic to the conormal sheaf of the diagonal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the canonical identification of the sheaf of relative differentials of f : X to S with the conormal sheaf of the diagonal immersion X to X times_S X (statement lines 6506-6511). The counted proof does two genuinely different things: it constructs the canonical map globally, by forming the square-zero thickening of the diagonal, exhibiting the conormal sheaf as the kernel of the resulting surjection, and then manufacturing the derivation as the difference of the two sections induced by the projections, which invokes the universal property of the module of differentials (proof lines 6515-6548); and it verifies the isomorphism over an affine chart U = Spec(A) over Spec(R), where the conormal sheaf becomes J/J^2 for the kernel of the multiplication of the tensor product algebra and the canonical map becomes the explicit formula sending a db to a tensor b minus ab tensor 1 (proof lines 6549-6593). It is H2: the final identification of the explicit formula is delegated to a cited algebra statement, but the construction of the map and the affine reduction are the author's own and are carried out in the counted span.
